title: Find the shortest way through a grid
prompt: grid is a list of rows of equal length. In each row "." is an open cell and "#" is a wall. Return the fewest moves needed to get from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell, moving one cell up, down, left or right at a time, through open cells only. Return 0 when the grid has one cell, and -1 when there is no way. The two corner cells are always open.
hints: This is a graph. What are its nodes, and which nodes are connected?
Each open cell is a node, connected to the open cells next to it. The fewest moves in such a graph is found by breadth-first search.
Keep the number of moves for each cell, with -1 for not reached. Start a queue with [0, 0]. For each cell, try the four neighbours that are inside the grid, open and not yet reached.
checkLabels: Going round the wall in the middle takes 4 moves.
Walls on both sides of the start leave no way.
A grid of one cell needs no moves.
The way round the walls takes 5 moves.
The only way goes down, up again, and down: 10 moves.

wrongAnswers.misconception: Moves only right and down, so it misses a way that has to go up or left.
Counts the cells on the way, including the start, instead of the moves between them.

feedback: Treat each open cell as a node and each pair of open cells side by side as a connection. Then it is the fewest-steps problem from the module on graphs.
